messages.text: Masters, Webb criticise FIFA over Balogun red card controversy

metadata.summary: Two of the most powerful men in English football have joined forces to hit out at FIFA and the U-turn which allowed USA striker Folarin Balogun to play on at the World Cup last month, despite the red card which should have led to an automatic ban.
metadata.content: Richard Masters and Howard Webb criticise FIFA over Folarin Balogun's red card controversy at 2026 World Cup | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Richard Masters and Howard Webb criticise FIFA over Folarin Balogun's red card controversy at 2026 World Cup USA striker Folarin Balogun had a red card suspended at the World Cup; it caused huge controversy after Donald Trump had called Gianni Infantino ahead of the last 32 match against Belgium; Balogun was sent off against Bosnia & Herzegovina and was suspended for two games Rob Dorsett Football Correspondent @RobDorsettSky Wednesday 19 August 2026 18:01, UK Image: Folarin Balogun was sent off against Bosnia & Herzegovina - but had his two-game ban controversially suspended Two of the most powerful men in English football have joined forces to hit out at FIFA and the U-turn which allowed USA striker Folarin Balogun to play on at the World Cup last month, despite the red card which should have led to an automatic ban. Richard Masters , the chief executive of the Premier League and Howard Webb , the chief refereeing officer in England, say the decision undermines faith in football at all levels of the game. Balogun was sent off in the last 32 match against Bosnia & Herzegovina which led to an automatic ban under World Cup rules, without the opportunity for appeal, or for the ban to be reduced.
